findings.documented: The API key must be appended as the api_key query parameter.
findings.actual: Protected API requests require the API key in the X-API-Key header; using only the documented query-parameter mechanism does not authenticate the request.
findings.how_found: Called protected endpoints with the documented query-parameter form, with X-API-Key only, and with X-API-Key plus a Bearer token, then compared the responses.
findings.impact: A client implemented strictly from the documentation cannot authenticate successfully.

findings.documented: A successful login returns token, token_type, expires_in and user.
findings.actual: Login returns access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expires_in, refresh_url and user; the documented token field is absent.
findings.how_found: Logged in with a valid demo account and inspected the complete response schema while redacting credential values.
findings.impact: A frontend reading the documented token field will fail to establish an authenticated session.

findings.documented: Access tokens are valid for 24 hours and expires_in is 86400.
findings.actual: The login API reports expires_in as 900 seconds.
findings.how_found: Inspected expires_in in successful login and refresh responses.
findings.impact: A frontend relying on the documented 24-hour lifetime can lose authentication long before expected unless it implements renewal.

findings.documented: There is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists, is advertised by login as refresh_url, accepts a refresh_token and returns authentication credentials.
findings.how_found: Used the refresh_url returned by login and successfully called POST /auth/refresh with the returned refresh token.
findings.impact: The actual mechanism required for a long-lived frontend session is missing from the documentation.

findings.documented: Logout invalidates the current token server side.
findings.actual: Logout returns a note that tokens are stateless and should be discarded client side; tested access tokens remained usable and the refresh token could still refresh after logout.
findings.how_found: Logged in, called logout, then retried protected requests with both access tokens and called the refresh endpoint again.
findings.impact: Clients must clear credentials locally and must not rely on logout for server-side token revocation.

findings.documented: Collection endpoints use 1-indexed page and limit parameters.
findings.actual: The running collection APIs use offset and limit. Supplying page=2 leaves offset at 0 and returns the first page again.
findings.how_found: Compared page=2&limit=5 with offset=5&limit=5 on listings, rentals and projects.
findings.impact: Following the documented paging algorithm repeats records and fails to retrieve the complete dataset.

findings.documented: The maximum collection limit is 200.
findings.actual: Requests with limit=200 are silently capped to limit=50 and return at most 50 records.
findings.how_found: Requested limit=200 from the collection endpoints and inspected the returned limit and count metadata.
findings.impact: Clients relying on the documented page size miscalculate the number of requests required to retrieve all records.

findings.documented: Collection responses contain total, page, page_size and results.
findings.actual: Collection responses contain limit, offset, count, total, has_more and results; page and page_size are absent.
findings.how_found: Inspected successful unfiltered collection responses from listings, rentals and projects.
findings.impact: Clients built against the documented pagination response schema cannot navigate the actual API correctly.

findings.documented: total is the exact number of records matching the request and can be used to determine when retrieval is complete.
findings.actual: The reported totals undercount retrievable records: listings reports 3201 but 3500 are retrievable, rentals reports 1207 but 1320 are retrievable, and projects reports 366 but 400 are retrievable.
findings.how_found: Ignored total as a stopping condition and continued paging with offset until has_more became false, then verified unique IDs in the complete snapshots.
findings.impact: A client that trusts total as documented stops early and silently loses records.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings returns active listings only; inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: The complete retrievable collection contains 3500 records, including 708 records where is_live is false.
findings.how_found: Paged to the true end of the listings collection and counted the boolean is_live values across the complete snapshot.
findings.impact: A frontend that assumes every returned record is active can display withdrawn or inactive properties to users.

findings.documented: The order parameter supports asc and desc for listing sorting.
findings.actual: Descending order is ignored. For tested sort fields, asc and desc returned identical listing IDs; price descending, for example, returned ascending prices.
findings.how_found: Requested the same listing sort fields with order=asc and order=desc and compared complete returned ID/value sequences.
findings.impact: Users asking for highest-priced or otherwise descending results receive the opposite/default order.

findings.documented: sort_by=carpet_area sorts listings by carpet area.
findings.actual: The returned carpet-area sequence is not monotonic in either raw values or the independently verified normalized square-foot values.
findings.how_found: Requested carpet_area ascending and descending, extracted all returned carpet-area values, and tested monotonicity before and after the verified Magichomes unit normalization.
findings.impact: Area-based browsing and ranking cannot rely on the server sort.

findings.documented: sort_by=posted_at sorts listings by their posted timestamp.
findings.actual: Results are not ordered by the full posted_at timestamp; records from the same date appear with times out of order, and descending returns the same sequence.
findings.how_found: Requested posted_at ascending and descending and compared parsed timestamp sequences.
findings.impact: A recent-first or oldest-first listings view built from the documented sort parameter is incorrect.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns a single listing.
findings.actual: The documented singular path returns HTTP 404 for known-valid listing IDs.
findings.how_found: Called the documented path using valid IDs sampled from the retrieved listings collection.
findings.impact: A detail page implemented exactly from the documentation cannot load a listing.

findings.documented: The documentation only specifies the singular detail path /v1/listing/{listing_id}.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings/{id} exists and returns the correct single listing object.
findings.how_found: Tested the plural-path counterpart after the documented singular path returned 404, using multiple known-valid listing IDs.
findings.impact: The working endpoint needed for the required listing-detail screen is absent from the documentation.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings.
findings.actual: The endpoint returns HTTP 404 for known-valid listing IDs.
findings.how_found: Called the documented similar-listings route for several valid listings retrieved from the collection.
findings.impact: The documented comparable-listings feature cannot be implemented using the promised endpoint.

findings.documented: Area values are square feet integers everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: A distinct cluster of 323 Magichomes listings stores carpet_area below 300 and super_built_up_area below 400 in metric-scale values. Converting these values from square metres to square feet aligns BHK area medians and price-per-square-foot distributions with the other sources.
findings.how_found: Compared area distributions by website and BHK, identified a source-specific discontinuity, converted the candidate cluster by 10.7639, and validated the converted medians against the other four websites.
findings.impact: Treating these values as square feet produces severely inflated price-per-square-foot values and incorrect area displays.

findings.documented: Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC values with a Z suffix everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: All 3500 retrievable listing posted_at values are timezone-naive strings such as 2026-08-19T10:52:00, with neither Z nor an explicit offset.
findings.how_found: Scanned posted_at across the complete listing snapshot and classified timezone suffixes before computing the fixed Q8 window.
findings.impact: Clients cannot determine the intended instant from the timestamp alone and can produce different date-window results depending on timezone interpretation.

findings.documented: Rental listings support sort_by together with order=asc or order=desc.
findings.actual: Descending order is ignored. Tested ascending and descending requests returned identical rental IDs; price descending still returned prices in ascending order.
findings.how_found: Requested rental sorting by price, bedroom and posted_at with both order directions and compared returned IDs and value monotonicity.
findings.impact: Rental ranking cannot reliably provide high-to-low or newest-first views using the documented server parameters.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are rupee amounts.
findings.actual: Project prices use mixed lakh/crore numeric scales rather than raw INR: values below 10 behave as crores while values in the tens behave as lakhs. Raw values produce 184 projects where price_min exceeds price_max; lakh/crore normalization reduces that count to zero.
findings.how_found: Examined project price distributions and inverted ranges, tested lakh/crore normalization, and validated normalized values against linked listing prices and server sort behaviour.
findings.impact: Displaying raw project prices as INR makes project prices wrong by orders of magnitude and can reverse min/max meaning.

findings.documented: Project sorting supports order=asc and order=desc.
findings.actual: Descending order is ignored for the tested project sort fields; asc and desc return identical project IDs.
findings.how_found: Compared asc and desc responses for price_min, price_max, launch_date and total_units and checked value monotonicity.
findings.impact: Highest-price, latest-launch and largest-project views cannot rely on the documented server-side descending sort.

findings.documented: total_listings is the number of listings currently available in each project and always agrees with the project's current listings.
findings.actual: For 106 of 400 projects, total_listings differs from the independently counted live associated listings.
findings.how_found: Joined the complete project snapshot to all retrievable listings by project_id, counted records with is_live=true for every project and compared those counts with total_listings.
findings.impact: Project availability counts shown to users are incorrect for more than one quarter of projects.

findings.documented: Project total_listings agrees with GET /v1/listings?project_id=..., implying project_id filters the listings collection to that project.
findings.actual: project_id is ignored. For project P60001, the request returned 50 records and all 50 belonged to other projects or had no project_id; the same unfiltered first page was returned for other project IDs.
findings.how_found: Queried several projects using project_id alone and project_id plus is_live=true, then compared every returned record's project_id with the requested project.
findings.impact: A frontend cannot use the documented project linkage query to show the listings belonging to a project.

findings.documented: Logged-in users can list, add and delete saved listings through GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}.
findings.actual: The favourites resource is absent. The documented GET and POST paths and DELETE resource path return framework-level HTTP 404 Not Found; the tested /v1/favorites, /v1/favourite and /v1/favorite variants also return HTTP 404.
findings.how_found: Tested the documented lifecycle with valid sessions for two demo users, then tested British/American singular and plural path variants.
findings.impact: The required saved-listings feature cannot be implemented using the documented backend and needs a client-side fallback.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed city aggregates including total listings, median price, median price per square foot, locality breakdown and BHK breakdown.
findings.actual: The documented endpoint returns HTTP 404 with detail Not Found both without credentials and with valid X-API-Key and Bearer credentials.
findings.how_found: Called the exact documented route before and after valid authentication.
findings.impact: The required Insights screen cannot obtain the promised aggregates from the documented backend endpoint and must compute them from retrieved data.

findings.documented: Listing records describe real property attributes that can be consumed by the application.
findings.actual: 18 listing records contain impossible property data: floor above total_floors, non-positive sale price, or carpet_area greater than super_built_up_area.
findings.how_found: Ran hard physical-validity checks across every retrievable listing and manually inspected each candidate record before finalizing the set.
findings.impact: Using these records in pricing, area statistics or property displays produces nonsensical results.

findings.documented: The sale listings represent genuine property listings and price is the property's sale price in INR.
findings.actual: Six records form an isolated ultra-low-price cluster with prices from 5030 to 26260 followed by a jump to 2730000; their values form an isolated ultra-low-price cluster inconsistent with genuine total sale prices rather than genuine total sale prices and identify the enquiry-generation listings.
findings.how_found: Examined the full positive-price distribution, detected the approximately 104x gap after the sixth record, then validated candidates using normalized area, peer prices, project price ranges, duplicate-property comparisons and contact patterns.
findings.impact: These records distort sale-price analytics and would expose users to deliberately non-genuine enquiry-generation listings.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: The IDs are unique, but the records are not one-to-one with physical properties. Normalized matching identified 240 duplicate-property groups containing 486 records; collapsing the duplicates reduces 3500 listing records to 3254 distinct properties.
findings.how_found: Normalized building names and the verified Magichomes area units, generated within-building candidate pairs, required matching structural attributes and close geographic agreement, rejected geographic outliers, and computed connected components.
findings.impact: Treating every listing record as a distinct property overcounts inventory by 246 properties and biases property-level analytics.
